My research is in **discrete, convex, and computational geometry**.

I am currently working with [Gregory Chambers](https://profiles.rice.edu/faculty/gregory-chambers){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} on problems in polyhedral geometry, including unfoldings of convex polyhedra. My broader interests include:

- Blocking and covering numbers of convex bodies and the [Hadwiger conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadwiger_conjecture_(combinatorial_geometry)){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}  
- Rigidity theory and applications of algebraic methods such as the theory of places, a tool used, for example, in the proof of the [Bellows Conjecture](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/BellowsConjecture.html){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}.

## Previous Research

Before joining the Department of Mathematics at Rice University, I worked with [Matthias Heinkenschloss](https://profiles.rice.edu/faculty/matthias-heinkenschloss){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} in Rice’s [Department of Computational Applied Mathematics and Operations Research](https://cmor.rice.edu/){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}. My research focused on parameter identifiability and local solution manifolds of nonlinear least squares problems.

### Undergraduate and Earlier Projects

- **Blocking Numbers of Convex Bodies**  
  Bachelor’s thesis at the Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology, supervised by [Alexander Polyanskii](https://polyanskii.com/){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}.

- **Max-sum Matchings of Points**  
  Undergraduate research project at MIPT, supervised by [Alexander Polyanskii](https://polyanskii.com/){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}.  
  The project focused on the [conjecture](https://ics.uci.edu/~eppstein/junkyard/maxmatch.html) posed by Andy Fingerhut in 1995, concerning the intersection of ellipses induced by a maximal-sum matching of an even set of points in the plane. The conjecture was later resolved by P. Barabanshchikova and A. Polyanskii in [*Intersecting Ellipses Induced by a Max-Sum Matching*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.14200){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}.

- **Rigidity of Laman Graphs and the Bellows Conjecture**  
  Research practicum thesis at MIPT, supervised by [Alexander Polyanskii](https://polyanskii.com/){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}.  
  I studied applications of the theory of places, an algebraic tool used in the proof of the Bellows Conjecture, and applied it to obtain a new proof of the rigidity of Laman graphs.
